purpose: AI-reviewed development source-claim and abstention set; not evaluation gold or training data

claims.source_span: Within Army combined arms doctrine, intelligence is a subset of relevant information.
claims.abstention_rationale: The subset claim is expressly limited to Army combined arms doctrine; the present CNL cannot retain that contextual scope.

claims.source_span: Intelligence is one of the warfighting functions that enables the Army to generate combat power during the conduct of operations.
claims.abstention_rationale: The tempting IntelligenceWarfightingFunction subclass-of WarfightingFunction claim is already in doctrine_domain.kif, so it cannot count as a source-derived positive.

claims.source_span: The Army intelligence process consists of four steps (plan and direct, collect and process, produce, and disseminate and integrate) and five continuing activities (synchronize, conduct intelligence operations, perform PED, analyze, and assess).
claims.abstention_rationale: The four-step and five-activity counts are central to this passage; the current CNL cannot state or verify the exact cardinalities.

claims.source_span: Assess is part of the overall assessment continuing activity of the operations process.
claims.abstention_rationale: The word part concerns an assessment activity within an operations process; replacing it with subclass or subProcess would impose an unverified kind-versus-part reading.

claims.source_span: Although all-source intelligence takes longer to produce, it is more reliable and less susceptible to deception than single-source intelligence.
claims.abstention_rationale: The comparison of production time, reliability, and susceptibility to deception requires comparative and defeasible structure absent from the CNL.

claims.source_span: Single-source intelligence includes the joint intelligence disciplines, which are also the Army intelligence disciplines, and when available (it can differ by echelon) and properly planned, the complementary capabilities from warfighting functions and branches other than intelligence.
claims.abstention_rationale: Complementary capabilities are included only when available and properly planned; an unconditional inclusion claim would lose both conditions.

claims.source_span: Open-source intelligence is intelligence that is produced from publicly available information and is collected, exploited, and disseminated in a timely manner to an appropriate audience for the purpose of addressing a specific intelligence requirement (Public Law 109-163).
claims.claim_text: Open-source intelligence, in the produced-intelligence sense, is an intelligence product.
claims.entailment_rationale: The definition explicitly describes intelligence that is produced from publicly available information; the separate class name is limited to the product sense.
omitted_qualifiers: The public-source provenance, timely collection and dissemination, audience, and specific requirement are omitted.
claims.notes: AI-reviewed development claim; not evaluation gold or a training example.

claims.source_span: Technical intelligence is intelligence derived from the collection, processing, analysis, and exploitation of data and information pertaining to foreign equipment and materiel for the purposes of preventing technological surprise, assessing foreign scientific and technical capabilities, and developing countermeasures designed to neutralize an enemy’s technological advantages (JP 2-0).
claims.claim_text: Technical intelligence, in its produced-intelligence sense, is an intelligence product.
claims.entailment_rationale: The definition explicitly describes intelligence derived from collection, processing, analysis, and exploitation; the class name is limited to that product.
omitted_qualifiers: The foreign-equipment subject matter and listed purposes are omitted.
claims.notes: AI-reviewed development claim; not evaluation gold or a training example.

claims.source_span: Biometrics is the process of recognizing an individual based on measurable anatomical, physiological, and behavioral characteristics (JP 2-0).
claims.claim_text: Biometrics, in its process sense, is a process.
claims.entailment_rationale: The cited sentence explicitly calls biometrics a process. The separate class name identifies only that process sense; the paragraph also uses biometrics for characteristics of an individual.
omitted_qualifiers: The recognition of an individual and the measurable anatomical, physiological, and behavioral characteristics that define the process are omitted. This claim must not be read as covering biometrics in its characteristics sense.
claims.notes: A deliberately minimal positive to exercise declaration/assertion separation. It is AI-reviewed development evidence, not an evaluation label or a training example.

claims.source_span: A cyberspace capability is a device or computer program, including any combination of software, firmware, or hardware, designed to create an effect in or through cyberspace (JP 3-12).
claims.abstention_rationale: A cyberspace capability may be a device or computer program. Choosing either branch as a universal subclass would be unsupported; the present CNL cannot express the disjunction.

claims.source_span: Document and media exploitation is the processing, translation, analysis, and dissemination of collected hardcopy documents and electronic media that are under the U.S. Government’s physical control and are not publicly available.
claims.abstention_rationale: DocumentAndMediaExploitation is already declared a subclass of Procedure in doctrine_domain.kif. Mapping it to Process through that background hierarchy would not be an independent source-derived positive.

claims.source_span: EW consists of three distinct divisions—electromagnetic attack (EA), electromagnetic support (ES), and electromagnetic protection (EP).
claims.abstention_rationale: The three divisions are named, but division does not by itself establish subclass or partTypes semantics, and the CNL has no verified division relation.

claims.source_span: Electromagnetic support is division of electromagnetic warfare involving actions tasked by, or under direct control of, an operational commander to search for, intercept, identify, and locate or localize sources of intentional and unintentional radiated electromagnetic energy for the purpose of immediate threat recognition, targeting, planning, and conduct of future operations (JP 3-85).
claims.abstention_rationale: Division of electromagnetic warfare may describe a component or category. The current ontology has no reviewed mapping for that sense.

claims.source_span: Forensic science is the application of multidisciplinary scientific processes to establish facts (DODD 5205.15E).
claims.abstention_rationale: Application of scientific processes does not entail that forensic science itself is a Process, Procedure, or Science in the SUMO senses without a reviewed mapping.
